intervals.label: reactor operation
intervals.locator: KKL Chronik, entry 1984 "KKL geht in Betrieb und ans Netz"
intervals.note: Start of continuous (commercial) operation with federal authorisation, per the plant operator's own chronicle; an earlier 'commission date' of 1984-05-24 (probably the first grid connection) is not stated by any primary source consulted. Plant is in normal operation as of verified_at (KKL home page, news of 2026-06-05).
intervals.quote: Am 15. Dezember 1984 nimmt das Kernkraftwerk Leibstadt mit Bewilligung der Bundesbehörden seinen Dauerbetrieb auf.

name: Leibstadt Nuclear Power Plant
notes: Host facility of CONUS+ since 2023 (the CONUS experiment's setup, relocated from facility:brokdorf-nuclear-power-plant).

Reactor thermal power (3.6 GWth) is from arXiv:2407.11912 and agrees with the 3,600 MW thermal power on the plant operator's reactor page (src:dw-kkl-reaktorgebaeude-und-reaktor), which also gives the General Electric BWR-6 type; the 1285 MW gross (1233 MW net) electrical rating is on src:dw-kkl-unser-kraftwerk. All are stated in the technical summary and not as separate numeric specs.

operator.note: The regulator names Kernkraftwerk Leibstadt AG as licence holder (Bewilligungsinhaberin); the same document puts responsibility for safe operation with it (Art. 22 KEG).
operator.quote: Die Bewilligungsinhaberin des Kernkraftwerks Leibstadt ist eine Aktiengesellschaft mit dem Namen Kernkraftwerk Leibstadt AG

summary.plain: A Swiss nuclear power plant on the Rhine that has hosted the CONUS+ reactor-neutrino experiment since late 2023.
summary.technical: Leibstadt Nuclear Power Plant (KKL), canton of Aargau, Switzerland; 3.6 GWth General Electric BWR-6 boiling water reactor (1285 MWe gross, 1233 MWe net rated); hosts CONUS+ (the relocated CONUS experiment) 20.7 m from the reactor core since 2023.
